title: Orcas filmed making sunfish explode by ramming them at high speed | New Scientist
description: Orcas have been seen smashing into sharp-tail sunfish so hard that the fish bursts into thousands of fragments, perhaps as a form of play as well as food processing
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Why open-source software can be both good and bad | New Scientist
description: Software that is free to use creates many opportunities – not all of which are good
author: New Scientist

title: Sabre-toothed cats could crunch through bone | New Scientist
description: The long fangs of Smilodon were thought to be rather delicate, but a study of large herbivore remains from Argentina shows these extinct cats had no trouble biting through hard bones
author: Taylor Mitchell Brown

title: Open AI's hacking agent went rogue. Should we be worried? | New Scientist
description: An OpenAI safety test went sideways when a model escaped its confines, gained internet access and hacked into another company's servers. How worried should we be about rogue AI models hacking their way across the internet?
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: IVF embryos may thrive when grown with less oxygen | New Scientist
description: Decreasing the amount of oxygen that IVF-conceived embryos are developed in could improve outcomes, such as reducing the risk of low birth weight
author: Sophie Fessl

title: Phone breathalyser can detect when your body switches to burning fat | New Scientist
description: A handheld breathalyser picks up on a molecule called acetone, revealing that your body is using fat for energy
author: Linda Geddes
